page.overview:
What is I'll Be On My Way?

5 December 1994 (US)|recorded=4 April 1963|genre=Pop|length=1:58|row6=Apple Records|songwriter=Lennon-McCartney|producer=Bryant Marriott, George Martin (Executive Producer)}}

I'll Be on My Way is a song attributed to the Lennon-McCartney writing partnership, although generally considered primarily a Paul McCartney composition with a strong Buddy Holly influence. Although never recorded by the Beatles for an official release, it was performed on 4 April 1963 for the BBC programme Side by Side, broadcast on 24 June. A recording sourced from this transmission was later included on the 1994 album Live at the BBC.

A recording of the song was first released by Billy J Kramer & the Dakotas on 26 April 1963 as the B-side of their debut single on Parlophone, "Do You Want to Know a Secret?" In addition to a record label, the act also shared the same manager, Brian Epstein, and producer, George Martin, as the Beatles. "I'll Be on My Way" was the first Lennon-McCartney song to be covered that the Beatles did not record themselves.

Mark Lewisohn dates the origins of the song to 1959, when McCartney first composed it on his Zenith 17. John Lennon always declared no association with the song, calling it "early Paul" in a 1972 interview and in 1980 stating it was "Paul, through and through. Doesn't it sound like him?" However, Richie Unterberger suggested that "one would guess that Lennon had at least some input into the writing" since they share lead vocals, "which rarely occurred on tunes that were solely the work of one or the other". McCartney's official biography, Many Years from Now, called the song co-written.
